Fit isodars

Source: R/fit_isodars.R
fit_isodars.Rd

Fits isodars to abundances (or densities) recorded in two or more habitats at a set of sites (or other replicates, such as years). Data are either in wide format (one species; one row per site, one column per habitat) or in long format (one or many species; one row per species x site x habitat).

Usage

fit_isodars(
  data,
  hab_cols = NULL,
  n_habitats = NULL,
  dim = c("pairwise", "ndim"),
  flip_intercept = TRUE,
  ndim_method = c("auto", "pca", "latent"),
  absent = "auto",
  absent_max_count = 0,
  absent_min_sites = 5,
  species = NULL,
  site = NULL,
  habitat = NULL,
  abundance = NULL,
  effort = NULL,
  reference_effort = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Wide format: one row per site and one numeric column per habitat; NA marks a habitat that is absent from, or was not sampled at, a site. Long format: one row per species x site x habitat (see Details).

hab_cols

Wide format: character vector of habitat column names.

n_habitats

Alternatively, the number of habitat columns, taken from the start of data. One of hab_cols or n_habitats is required.

dim

"pairwise" or "ndim".

flip_intercept

Pairwise only. If TRUE, an isodar with a negative intercept and positive slope is expressed in the reverse direction (habitats swapped), so that intercepts are non-negative.

ndim_method

"auto", "pca" or "latent"; see Details.

absent

Habitats the species does not use: "auto" (detected from the data, see Details), "none", or a character vector of habitat names (character(0) is the same as "none").

absent_max_count, absent_min_sites

Thresholds for absent = "auto"; see Details.

species, site, habitat, abundance, effort

Long format: names of the columns holding species (optional; without it the data are one species), site (or other replicate), habitat, abundance (counts) and sampling effort (optional; without it every row has effort 1).

reference_effort

Long format: the sampling unit in which densities are expressed (default: median effort); see Details.

Value

For dim = "pairwise", a tibble of class isodars_pairwise with one row per pair of used habitats: habitat_x, habitat_y, intercept, slope, sd (SD of perpendicular residuals), n_sites, and flipped (whether the habitats were swapped). For dim = "ndim", a tibble of class isodar_line with one row per habitat: habitat, mean, direction (both 0 for absent habitats); attributes var_explained (share of variance along the line, "pca" only), eigenvalues, n_sites and ndim_method. Both have attributes habitats (all habitats), absent and undersampled.

In long format, a tibble of class isodar_fits with one row per species: species (if given), fit (the fit as above, or NULL if it failed), counts and effort (site x habitat matrices), n_sites and note (warnings and errors from fitting). One summary warning is given if any species could not be fitted.

Details

Input formats. In wide format, give hab_cols (or n_habitats); the values are used as they are, and the result is a single fit. In long format, give the column names site, habitat and abundance (and optionally species and effort); the result is an isodar_fits table with one row per species, which niche_breadth() and iai_curve() take. Replicates may be sites or time steps (for example, years at one site); in long format they go in the site column. A site x habitat combination that appears for any species is taken as sampled, and a species without a row there has 0 individuals there; a habitat missing at a site simply has no rows. Sites where a species has no individuals in any habitat carry no information on its habitat selection and are dropped for that species.

Effort and densities. Isodars relate densities. In long format, density = abundance / effort x reference_effort. Effort may be an area, a transect length (constant width) or a unitless relative effort, but must be the same kind of measure in every row; it must be the same for every row of a site x habitat combination. reference_effort (default: the median effort of sampled site x habitat combinations) is the sampling unit in which abundances are expressed: "one individual" in the density-independent niche breadth, the spillover abundance and the x-axis of iai_curve() all mean one individual per reference_effort. Density-independent niche breadth and spillover abundance therefore depend on this unit; slopes and density-dependent niche breadth do not. The default depends on how samples happen to be pooled, so set reference_effort to a natural unit (for example, the area of one standard transect) and use the same value for every species you compare.

In wide format, rows are used as given: unlike long format, a site with 0 in every habitat is kept (it pulls the isodars toward the origin), so remove such rows if they mean the species was absent from the site.

Pairwise isodars (dim = "pairwise") are fitted for every pair of habitats by total least squares (TLS), which is identical to major-axis regression in two dimensions. Each pair uses every site where both habitats were recorded (non-missing), so sites lacking some habitats still contribute. When many sites are incomplete, both pairwise isodars and the latent line (below) use all of them; fitting both is a useful check.

The n-dimensional isodar (dim = "ndim") is a line. Under the ideal free distribution, equal fitness across \(n\) habitats imposes \(n-1\) equalities, so abundances across habitats change along a single line as total abundance changes, whatever the number of habitats. The line is described by a point (mean) and a unit direction vector (direction), with one component per habitat. Each component is the rate at which that habitat gains individuals as total abundance rises (the analogue of the isodar slope); where the line enters each habitat reflects its density-independent preference (the analogue of the intercept). Every pairwise isodar can be derived from it, and with two habitats it is the classic isodar.

With ndim_method = "pca" the line is the first principal axis of the covariance matrix of complete sites (the TLS line). With ndim_method = "latent" it is estimated from all sites with at least two recorded habitats, as a one-factor model, \(N_{hs} = \mu_h + v_h t_s + \varepsilon_{hs}\), where \(t_s\) is the position of site \(s\) along the isodar (requires glmmTMB). ndim_method = "auto" uses "pca" when every site is complete and "latent" otherwise.

Absent habitats. A habitat that the species never uses carries no information about habitat selection, and an isodar cannot be fitted to it. Such a habitat is excluded from the fit and fixed at 0 abundance; iai() still counts it, as 0, in the inequality, so it lowers niche breadth. With absent = "auto" a habitat is declared absent if the species was recorded in it no more than absent_max_count times in total (in the units of wide data; as counts, before conversion to densities, in long format), and the habitat was sampled at no fewer than absent_min_sites sites where the species was present in another habitat. A habitat with (almost) no records but fewer such sites is undersampled: it is kept in the fit, with a warning, because its zeros may reflect too little sampling rather than avoidance. A habitat used at low density and abandoned at high density is not absent; it is fitted, and iai() clips it to 0 at totals where the isodars predict negative abundance. With the default absent_max_count = 0, a single individual makes a habitat used, which can change the spillover abundance a lot; raise absent_max_count if a few stray individuals should not count.

Absent habitats lower niche breadth, so species should be compared over the same set of habitats, namely the habitats available to them.

References

Morris, D.W. (1987). Spatial scale and the cost of density-dependent habitat selection. Evolutionary Ecology, 1, 379–388.

See also

niche_breadth(), iai(), isoderr()

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_isodars(1.5, 1.5, 5, 5, noise = 1, n = 30)
fit_isodars(sim, hab_cols = c("hab1", "hab2", "hab3"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   habitat_x habitat_y intercept slope    sd n_sites flipped
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <int> <lgl>  
#> 1 hab1      hab2           5.18  1.50 0.649      30 FALSE  
#> 2 hab1      hab3          13.0   2.24 0.958      30 FALSE  
#> 3 hab2      hab3           5.24  1.50 0.723      30 FALSE  
fit_isodars(sim, hab_cols = c("hab1", "hab2", "hab3"), dim = "ndim")
#> n-dimensional isodar (line), method: pca | sites: 30 
#> Variance along the line: 0.999 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   habitat  mean direction
#>   <chr>   <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 hab1     28.8     0.348
#> 2 hab2     48.3     0.521
#> 3 hab3     77.5     0.780

# long format, several species
fish <- moorea_fish[moorea_fish$species %in% c("Acanthurus nigrofuscus",
  "Scarus schlegeli", "Zebrasoma scopas"), ]
fits <- fit_isodars(fish, species = "species", site = "site",
                    habitat = "habitat", abundance = "abundance")
fits
#> Isodars (pairwise) for 3 species; habitats: barrier_reef, fringing_reef, outer_slope; reference effort: 1
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   species                fit                counts   effort   n_sites note 
#>   <chr>                  <list>             <list>   <list>     <int> <chr>
#> 1 Acanthurus nigrofuscus <isdrs_pr [3 × 7]> <dbl[…]> <dbl[…]>      13 ""   
#> 2 Scarus schlegeli       <isdrs_pr [3 × 7]> <dbl[…]> <dbl[…]>      13 ""   
#> 3 Zebrasoma scopas       <isdrs_pr [3 × 7]> <dbl[…]> <dbl[…]>      13 ""   
fits$fit[[which(fits$species == "Scarus schlegeli")]]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   habitat_x     habitat_y    intercept    slope    sd n_sites flipped
#>   <chr>         <chr>            <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>   <int> <lgl>  
#> 1 fringing_reef barrier_reef     27.0   0.654   52.3       13 TRUE   
#> 2 barrier_reef  outer_slope       1.78 -0.00259  1.37      13 FALSE  
#> 3 fringing_reef outer_slope       1.94 -0.00330  1.34      13 FALSE
